summary: Make governed artifact identity stable across Git line-ending conversion while binding dirty and untracked files to their actual Git-canonical content.
reason: The execution-gate target-state calculation is a completion control. Raw working-tree byte hashing made the same committed Git content acquire different identities after checkout line-ending conversion. Revision 1 corrected that by hashing actual governed files through Git's path-aware clean/EOL filters, but Adversarial review found that git hash-object follows filesystem symlinks while Git stores symlink blobs as link-target text. That could make a governed symlink receive a non-Git-canonical identity. The bounded revision-2 correction fails closed on governed symlink paths, preserves deterministic ABSENT state and repository-containment checks, binds dirty and untracked regular files to their actual Git-canonical content, fails closed when Git identity cannot be established, and does not rewrite historical review evidence.
